body: Mario Golf: Advance Tour is Camelot's Game Boy Advance sports role-playing game following a young golfer through training, club tournaments and the ambition of eventually playing against Mario. Choosing Neil or Ella supplies the protagonist, with the other character becoming a doubles partner. Exploring the clubs gives the matches a setting beyond the course itself, connecting practice and conversation with a developing sporting career. The handheld adventure gives the player a particular golfer to improve, making the next tournament both a test of control and another stage in that character's progress toward stronger opponents.

Neil and Ella begin with different strengths in power, precision and shot shape. Training and competition provide ways to develop the chosen golfer, connecting the role-playing structure with the practical decisions made before each stroke. The player still has to read the course and choose an appropriate shot, but the character's capabilities shape what can reliably be attempted. A more ambitious route may become useful as the golfer improves. Development therefore creates new opportunities rather than automatically removing the need to understand the terrain and execute the next swing with care.

Marion, Palms, Dunes and Links each offer a course, practice facilities and places where the golfers stay. Winning their tournaments establishes the player's reputation and opens the way toward the larger goal. Moving around these clubs gives the campaign a rhythm of preparation, conversation and competition rather than presenting every match as an isolated menu choice. The connection with Mario's world remains a destination to work toward, allowing the early human cast and its smaller sporting ambitions to occupy a meaningful part of the adventure before the more familiar competitors arrive.
